nodes.title: Read-through of the 156 simpler and why sentences two Sonnet agents wrote for the 30 staged scripts (all had passed check.mjs; Learning had read 3 topics). A fresh Opus agent that wrote none of them read all 156 against their problem and board with three questions (true? simpler than what it replaces? gives the answer away?): 73 failed (67 not simpler, mostly near-copies of the problem; 3 not true; 4 language; 0 giveaways). All 73 were rewritten; a second fresh agent read the rewrites: 9 failed (3 not simpler, 2 not true, 4 language), fixed and read by Learning only. Totals: 156 read, 82 fixed. Learning ae9d5be55.

Sentences that pass the script gates fail a reader about half the time: 73 of 156 agent-written simplers and whys (47%) failed an independent read, 3 of them untrue. The gates check form (length, slots, numbers on the board), not whether a sentence is simpler or true. So 'nothing a child hears that nobody read' is a measured need, and a rewrite needs its own read (9 of 73 rewrites failed again).
